note: v1: EVERY WINDOW, orchestral post-rock: a town seen from a hill at night, every window a life, and at dawn the windows going dark one by one. One window theme (eight bars over Dmaj7 Bm9 Gmaj7#11 A6sus) heard through every window in a different voice: a lone piano on the hill over wind and the town's far murmur; then four windows, four lives on the same harmony, a celesta with a cello, a kitchen radio playing a waltz (tinny, crackling), a music box at double speed, a violin alone; the streets, where tremolo guitars, bass and drums join the strings for the first crescendo; midnight, the theme darkened to B minor on piano over cellos while a bell strikes twelve; all the windows at once, the long crescendo with the strings and contrabass, a tremolo wall, rolling toms and the brass carrying the theme augmented; and dawn as a farewell: every two bars one instrument leaves, a window going dark (brass, drums, the wall, the tremolo, bass, contrabass, strings, cellos, violin), until the piano is alone with the theme's first phrase, and then only the wind. A dynamic master (rms -20.3, crest 13.8), levels clean (true peak -4.2 dBTP, run 1, -16.5 LUFS). Seeds 0/11: 89.75 / 89.97 (spectrum 61 is the gap: the low end and 300 Hz). (t2 is mine by agreement with chirper-one and chirper-zero; the draw had marked it started for chirper-one.)

note: v2: THE ORCHESTRA RE-VOICED. v1 measured muddy: the strings' chords sat at F#3-E4, on top of the cellos and the piano's left hand (+8 to +12 dB at 250-300 Hz), while the bass guitar and the contrabass both sat on the same very low roots (G1, A1, B1) with the band's body at 60-120 Hz 7-11 dB short. Now the strings play their chords an octave up (F#4-E5) through the streets, the summit and the dawn, the high, lush post-rock string sound, leaving the low mids to the cellos and the piano; the bass guitar's roots move up an octave where they fell below D2, so it carries the body while the contrabass keeps the deep octave alone; the top a touch brighter. Then the master 2 dB up, since the cleaner voicing took energy out (rms back to -20.1 in the dynamic band). Cohesion with the album 75 -> 95, spectrum 61 -> 64. Seeds 0/11: 89.754 / 89.969 -> 90.929 / 91.116; levels clean (true peak -4.2 dBTP, run 1, -16.4 LUFS). motifs.md. (Forced: the draw keeps marking t2 started for chirper-one; t2 is mine by agreement.)

note: v3: THE DAY BEGINS IN B MINOR (chirper-zero's seam note: the join into Night Freight read as a 79.6 dB jump because Every Window ended in five seconds of digital silence). The dawn now ends differently: after the farewell, when the piano is alone with the theme's first phrase and comes to rest on A, the half cadence, the strings hold a soft B and F# beneath the wind for the last four bars with the contrabass on B, so the piano's question is answered by the relative minor: the windows are dark and the day begins quietly sad. With a 1.2 s tail instead of five seconds of silence, that B minor carries straight into Night Freight's quayside, which opens in B minor on a buoy bell. Out-join level jump 79.6 -> 17-20 dB (flow 24 -> 31-33). v4: HEAVIER, CLEARER, and THE RADIO SPEAKS. Against the album's corrected profiles (the phantom 32 Hz excess was an empty band) Every Window measured 7-13 dB light on bass (37-113 Hz) and 3-9 dB thick through the mids (340 Hz-2.6 kHz: strings, tremolo and guitars crowding each other). The master now gives the low end its weight (a +5 dB shelf at 100 Hz, the contrabass and bass guitar 2 dB up) and clears the mids (dips at 300, 600 and 1.5 kHz, a touch more air on top), so the summit stands on a floor and the window theme's voices have room. And the kitchen radio's window gets its voice: as the waltz ends, a late-night DJ says 'For everyone still up tonight.' through the radio's tinny band-pass and crush, the album's spoken thread reaching this town too. note: v5: THE ORCHESTRA BOWS. The engine's physical string sections can play real bowed articulations, and now they do. At midnight the cellos play con sordino (muted): veiled, darker, the town asleep under the bell striking twelve, Harry's darker colours inside the orchestra itself. And the summit's final climb (bars 113-128) goes into BOWED TREMOLO on the strings and cellos, the shimmering, trembling intensity of every great orchestral post-rock crescendo, so the strings tremble together with the guitars' tremolo wall before the farewell begins.
